name: Press pitch preparation
summary: An owner or marketer with one story to offer gets the outlets and writers it genuinely fits, each backed by a piece they recently published, and a short pitch draft for each. Every claim in a draft comes from facts you supply. Drafts only: a person decides and sends.

sources.title: Its own press guide, used in its marketing work: support labelled by kind (method, view, observed work, measured result), a story that holds at any time needs no invented news, outlets chosen from their own editorial guidance and a recent piece, a recipient's role rather than a guessed address, limits kept in the copy, and no exclusivity or availability promised without a basis.

sources.contribution: Whether a story is worth offering at all (a real story, someone to speak, a destination) and a check of each pitch before it goes: the writer covers the subject, the subject line is specific, the body is short and the ask is clear; and, from its section on when something goes wrong, the reason an incident or complaint is not met with a pitch: it needs confirmed facts, one accountable spokesperson and, where it matters, qualified advice.

Reading a writer's recent pieces before pitching, judging fit on subject, readers and recency, the order of a pitch ending in one ask, a short body, a subject line that names the story, no attachments and no hype words, not pitching a writer or outlet on what it says it does not take, and a follow-up only when it adds something new.
The product as evidence for a story rather than the story itself, a milestone needing a change or lesson around it, and an angle that stands against a broken practice, never a named competitor.
